title: Study Finds How a High-Calorie Diet May Affect the Brain
paragraphs: We already know that high-calorie diets can cause obesity and are linked with illnesses like type 2 diabetes. But there is growing evidence that these diets may affect healthy brain function as well.
Studies have, in particular, linked high-calorie diets with poorer cognitive performance and an increased risk of conditions like Alzheimer's disease.
To better understand what may be causing this, researchers from the Institute of Science Tokyo looked at the effect of a high-calorie diet on mice.
Their study, published in Molecular Psychiatry, revealed how a high-calorie diet could be linked to altered brain function and cognitive impairment.

The researchers fed mice a diet that was high in fat — which is incredibly calorie-dense — for either one or six weeks. Then they compared the nerve cells of these mice with those that ate a normal diet.

They found that the mice on a high-fat diet had reduced levels of a protein called PQBP1 in their cerebral cortex — an area of the brain that supports cognitive functioning. PQBP1 regulates the production of other proteins that are necessary for the brain's nerve cells to work properly.

When they looked closer, the researchers found that higher levels of insulin — a hormone that manages blood sugar levels — among the mice on a high-fat diet had restricted the production of PQBP1. The result was an overall decline in healthy brain activity.
However, the researchers also found a way to reverse this damage, which may have positive implications for human health too.

Some mice that were fed a high-fat diet were also treated with pioglitazone, a drug used for diabetes management. The researchers found that the medication brought PQBP1 levels back to normal, and improved cognitive function.
They also had success in using gene therapy to restore PQBP1 and fix brain function problems.
So, while the study revealed the potential dangers of a high-calorie diet for brain health, it also found possible effective approaches for treating some of the negative impacts.
